justification: The recursive-tool-smithing plugin implements a safety-sandboxed evolution loop that requires subprocess execution to run candidate scripts under a hard 5-minute timeout. The sandbox_runner.py script uses subprocess.run with capture_output=True and a timeout parameter as the ENFORCEMENT mechanism for the Mode-Invariant Compliance Gate - it is the safety boundary, not a bypass of it. All subprocess calls are static (no shell=True, no user-controlled arguments in the command array). No network calls are permitted within the sandbox; the subprocess constraint only applies to the outer runner orchestrating the isolated evaluation.

whitelisted_operations.reason: Executes candidate toolbox scripts under controlled timeout enforcement. Arguments are never user-supplied at runtime - always ['python3', <static_script_path>]. No shell=True.
Reads git branch/commit state for boot digest generation. Read-only git commands: git rev-parse, git status --porcelain. No writes.
Executes git add and git commit after a toolbox script passes the sandbox gate and graduated autonomy check. Only runs after explicit keep classification.
whitelisted_operations.scope: git add + git commit only, within scripts/toolbox/

forbidden_operations: network access from within sandbox (requests, httpx, urllib)
subprocess calls from within generated toolbox scripts
eval() or exec() with dynamic input
